matched.label: Black Loyalist
matched.note: Current term for people who arrived in Nova Scotia after the American Revolution and were recorded in the Book of Negroes and related registers.

language_bridge.status: Draft terminology map for community review. Not an authoritative vocabulary.

record.title: Book of Negroes, 1783
record.description: Register of Black people who evacuated New York on British ships to Nova Scotia from April to November 1783, following the American Revolution. Library and Archives Canada holds a searchable database of 2,831 references from the register.
record.original_id: Book of Negroes, MG23 B1, microfilm M-369
record.access_information: Search the database and view the digitized register through Library and Archives Canada.

records.content_note: 'Book of Negroes' is the historical title of the 1783 register and is kept so the record can be found. The word is outdated and offensive today; THREADS uses it only to match the source's own title.

record.title: Black Loyalist Refugees, 1782-1807
record.description: Records relating to Black Loyalist refugees who arrived in Nova Scotia between 1782 and 1807, held in the Port Roseway Associates series at Library and Archives Canada.
record.access_information: View digitized material through Canadiana Heritage; consult Library and Archives Canada for the full series.

record.title: Muster Book of Free Black Settlement of Birchtown, Port Roseway, 1784
record.description: Register created in the summer of 1784 listing the names and ages of Black men, women, and children who established the settlement of Birchtown, near Shelburne, Nova Scotia, with details of professions, military rank, and family ties where recorded.
record.original_id: Muster Book of Free Black Settlement of Birchtown, Port Roseway, R16987, MG9 B9-14
record.access_information: View the digitized register through Canadiana Heritage, linked from Library and Archives Canada.

record.title: Carleton Papers, British Headquarters Papers, 1774-1783
record.description: British Headquarters Papers, New York, including the Carleton Papers. Library and Archives Canada holds a microfilm copy and a searchable index covering loyalist soldiers and civilian refugees.
record.access_information: Search the index through Library and Archives Canada; consult the access options on the source page for copies and microfilm.
